output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly not caused by release 6.14. At 10:41 UTC on 3 March, a new vendor rule (AUTO-LIB-17) in the edge protection service began blocking Android password logins. The rule matches the app's networking library signature on the password path. About 41,300 real installs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before. The failures are HTTP 403 rejections that began within one minute on every app version, every Android OS version, and with or without the March security patch. Quick-unlock is unaffected, and iOS and web don't use that library signature. The 6.14 rollout was only 5% of attempts, and its success rate matches the other versions. Credential-stuffing, OS patches, the new password screen, and the token-lifetime change don't fit the evidence. Next step: ask Corvane to set the new rules to log-only on the mobile password-login path. Keep rate limits, lockout and other rules on. Then confirm password-login success recovers to its pre-3 March level. Don't roll back 6.14, don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't drop blocked attempts from the KPI. Those would hide or worsen the problem. Confidence is high. The remaining uncertainty is how much the credential-stuffing on 28 February still matters.
